@graph.name: Bag Case Packer
@graph.description: A bag case packer is a top-load machine that collates filled flexible bags, such as VFFS, IQF, pet food and grated cheese bags, and loads them into shipping cases in a repeatable count and pattern. TRF Industrial Automation packs these bags with TRFDroppack, its gravity drop packer. Pouches and pillow bags can also be packed with TRFRapidpack, and pillow bags with TRFOnepack, when the line calls for robotic handling.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Throughput Range of a Gravity Case Packer?

acceptedAnswer.text: TRFDroppack is designed for applications of about 20 to 500 products per minute, for lines that need gravity loading without robotic complexity. TRF publishes application ranges, not machine speeds: actual capacity depends on the bag, the collation, the drop path, the pack pattern and the case, and TRF engineering validates it with your real bags before the design is closed.

mainEntity.name: Does a Case Packer Need Vision-Guided Robotics for High-Mix Production?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only when bag position varies or the line runs many formats. TRFRapidpack picks with vision-guided delta robots when bags reach the packer in a random flow, and with indexed picking when they arrive in fixed lanes. Repetitive bags in standardized patterns usually need neither, which is where TRFDroppack and its controlled gravity loading fit.

mainEntity.name: Do All Bags Need to Be Packed in Cases Before Palletizing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Many large bags and sacks ship directly on pallets without a shipping case, which makes them a palletizing application rather than a case packing one. TRF covers both: case packing with TRFDroppack, TRFRapidpack or TRFOnepack, and direct palletizing on the bag palletizer page, with the gripper and pallet pattern engineered for each bag.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between a Case Packer and a Case Erector?

acceptedAnswer.text: A case erector forms an open case from a flat blank, and a case packer loads products into that case. TRF supplies case erecting only as part of an integrated solution: TRFOnepack erects, packs and seals in one machine, and end-of-line projects include case forming and closing, so one partner answers for the flow from flat case to sealed case.

mainEntity.name: How Fast Can a Case Packer Change Over Between SKUs?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on how different the bags, patterns and cases are. On TRFRapidpack, product and pattern changes are recipe-based with reduced mechanical adjustments. On TRFDroppack, there is no robotic tooling to change, and the changeover plan for the formats the line runs is set during engineering. Count how many changeovers you run per week, because that number shapes the choice.

mainEntity.name: Can Case Packing Equipment Integrate With My Existing Palletizer and Conveyors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Each TRF case packing platform can run standalone or integrate with conveyors, case handling, palletizing and intralogistics as one end-of-line system. TRFIntraflow moves and accumulates packed cases to a TRFCobot, TRFCompact or TRFSpeed palletizer, and interfaces with your bagger and existing equipment are defined during project engineering. See end-of-line integration.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Typical ROI of Switching From Manual to Robotic Case Packing?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no typical figure, because payback depends on your plant. The estimate compares the installed cost of the system with the annual savings: packers per shift, shifts per day, local labor cost, the output the bagger gains when the packing table stops limiting it, damaged bags and rejected cases avoided, and time saved at changeovers. A TRF Sales Engineer builds it with your data.
